hypothesis: In fast-mode decode, using a token's five likeliest routed experts and the rest of its top-8 only when they are already in memory reads fewer experts from the SSD, so decode steps 2 to 32 after a 512-token prompt of code.txt get faster on an 8 GB M1, both versions fed the same tokens (teacher forcing), at a quality cost that is measured and stated.
model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration) converted to Colibri's qwen36 container: INT4 routed experts with gs=64 group scales, f16 dense weights (quantized to INT8 at load) and f16 embedding; 23 GB of safetensors; canonical.qc beside it (1.94 GB, written by qwen36-canonical) and experts.qc (17.1 GB, scales as 16-bit codes, the bytes qwen36-canonical --experts writes: its records written on 2026-10-05, its 8-byte stamp on 2026-10-07); the checkpoint's shards were written on 2026-09-16
command: git archive f2aa1165 c | tar -x -C <dir>, make -C <dir>/c qwen36_metal.o backend_metal.o METAL=1, then from the repository root, with the compiler flags make -C c qwen36 METAL=1 gives qwen36.c except its qpack path (-DQWEN36_QPACK and its objects, which the harness does not use): clang -O3 -Xclang -fopenmp -I<libomp>/include -Wall -Wextra -Wno-unused-parameter -Wno-misleading-indentation -Wno-unused-function -DCOLI_METAL -DQWEN36_METAL -I<dir>/c docs/experiments/qwen36-fast-experts-2026-10-06/bench.c <dir>/c/qwen36_metal.o <dir>/c/backend_metal.o -o <dir>/qwen36-bench -lm -L<libomp>/lib -lomp -framework Metal -framework Foundation -framework Accelerate -lc++; every run: /usr/bin/time -l env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin HOME=$HOME SNAP=<model> TEACHER=1 <dir>/qwen36-bench code.txt 64,512 32; baseline = the defaults, trial = QWEN36_FAST_EXPERTS=5, through launchers/fast5/qwen36-bench, a script with the one line QWEN36_FAST_EXPERTS=5 exec bin-pr10/qwen36-bench "$@"

hardware.cpu: Apple M1, 4 performance + 4 efficiency cores (MacBook Air, MacBookAir10,1, no fan)

config.SNAP: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Colibri qwen36 container, INT4 experts gs=64, internal SSD
config.BUILD: the compiler flags of make -C c qwen36 METAL=1 on macOS without its qpack path: clang -O3 -Xclang -fopenmp -DCOLI_METAL -DQWEN36_METAL, qwen36_metal.o and backend_metal.o
config.EXPERT_CACHE: the Metal graph's default: a sixteenth of the RAM (512 MiB, 303 slots of 1.77 MB)
config.PROMPT: the first 64 and the first 512 tokens of code.txt (in this record: an earlier version of c/qwen36_graph.h, 69,605 bytes, of which the harness reads the first 20,480; prompt_hash is its SHA-256), each from an empty state; after each, 32 tokens, each fed the text's own next token (teacher forcing: both versions read the same tokens)
config.ORDER: 1 warm-up run (baseline, discarded), then baseline trial trial baseline baseline trial trial baseline, one process each
config.REST: thermal state nominal, then 60 s, before every run
config.QWEN36_FAST_EXPERTS: unset: every chosen expert is used
config.MEASURED: tokens per second of decode steps 2 to 32 after the 512-token prompt, each step fed the text's next token (teacher forcing)

quality.method: Correctness: both versions were fed the same tokens (teacher forcing: the hash of the tokens is the same in every run of both), and without the variable this commit's exact-mode logits are its parent's (fingerprints.txt). The quality cost is measured, not gated: over 1024 teacher-forced tokens of this text after a 512-token prompt (quality.txt), J = 5 changes the mean negative log-likelihood by -0.67% (standard error 0.39%; perplexity -1.6%) and the share of tokens the model ranks first by -0.7 points (standard error 0.5). Fingerprints (baseline / trial), each the same in every run of its version: 64 tokens 2ca892c20f9dfdfa/24b5cd77c9db23fb / 22836d6252261251/24b5cd77c9db23fb, 512 tokens 31fb860c5d30aac5/561100505ac9d4ca / 0261c289646a535f/561100505ac9d4ca.
